course_title: Practical Exercise on European and Global Legal History
title: Exercise class 1: introduction, the method of exegesis, ancient legal cultures

slides.title: What is law — five theoretical answers
slides.text: The exercise class gives not one definition but FIVE SCHOOLS AND THEIR CRITERION. People have been occupied with law for millennia without ever agreeing on WHAT LAW IS. (1) LAW AS A BODY OF NORMS — HANS KELSEN AND THE VIENNA SCHOOL OF LEGAL THEORY: legal norms are compared with other norms (moral, religious) in order to establish WHAT DISTINGUISHES THEM; the answer is STATE-ORGANIZED COERCION. (2) LAW AS THE ACTUAL BEHAVIOUR OF CERTAIN GROUPS OF PEOPLE — OLIVER WENDELL HOLMES and the LEGAL REALISTS: 'THE PROPHECIES OF WHAT THE COURTS WILL DO IN FACT ARE WHAT I MEAN BY THE LAW'; this is called NORM SCEPTICISM. (3) LAW AS THE NECESSARY RESULT OF A HISTORICAL DEVELOPMENT that proceeds according to certain regularities — the HISTORICAL SCHOOL OF LAW. (4) LAW AS A CULTURAL PHENOMENON, that is, an expression of the relations of production (MARXIST THEORIES), of politics (POLICY SCIENCE) or of economics (LAW AND ECONOMICS). (5) LAW AS AN INSTRUMENT SERVING A PARTICULAR PURPOSE — SOCIOLOGICAL JURISPRUDENCE and JURISPRUDENCE OF INTERESTS; MAX WEBER understands law as an 'INNER SPIRITUAL FORCE OPERATING WITHIN PEOPLE', enforced by an EXTERNAL POWER, typically state authority, in order to order coexistence and resolve conflicts.

terms.def: Scepticism about the norm: law is what the courts actually do, not what the text says (Holmes, the legal realists).

cards.q: How do Kelsen and the Vienna school define law?
cards.a: As a BODY OF NORMS compared with other norms (moral, religious) in order to establish WHAT DISTINGUISHES THEM — and the answer is STATE-ORGANIZED COERCION.
cards.topic: Introduction: Methods, Sources, Aims of Legal History

cards.q: What is law according to Holmes and the legal realists?
cards.a: THE ACTUAL BEHAVIOUR OF CERTAIN GROUPS OF PEOPLE: 'THE PROPHECIES OF WHAT THE COURTS WILL DO IN FACT ARE WHAT I MEAN BY THE LAW.' This is called NORM SCEPTICISM.
cards.topic: Introduction: Methods, Sources, Aims of Legal History

cards.q: Name the five theoretical answers to the question what law is.
cards.a: 1) A BODY OF NORMS distinguished by state coercion (KELSEN). 2) ACTUAL BEHAVIOUR, that is, the prediction of what courts will decide (HOLMES, the realists). 3) THE NECESSARY RESULT OF HISTORICAL DEVELOPMENT (the historical school). 4) A CULTURAL PHENOMENON — an expression of the relations of production (Marxism), of politics or of economics. 5) AN INSTRUMENT SERVING A PURPOSE (sociological jurisprudence, jurisprudence of interests, Weber).
cards.topic: Introduction: Methods, Sources, Aims of Legal History

cards.q: How does Max Weber understand law?
cards.a: As an 'INNER SPIRITUAL FORCE OPERATING WITHIN PEOPLE', enforced by an EXTERNAL POWER, typically state authority, in order to ORDER COEXISTENCE AND RESOLVE CONFLICTS.
cards.topic: Introduction: Methods, Sources, Aims of Legal History

slides.title: Pufendorf against Kelsen: natural law and positivism
slides.text: The exercise class sets these two positions directly against each other, so it is worth remembering them as a pair. SAMUEL PUFENDORF (1632–1694): the idea of a LEGAL AND JUST ORDER DERIVED PURELY FROM REASON — and because it is derived from reason, it is UNALTERABLE BY HUMAN BEINGS and applies EQUALLY AND EVERYWHERE ON EARTH. This is NATURAL LAW or the LAW OF REASON, whose line can be traced back to ARISTOTLE. HANS KELSEN (1881–1973): LAW IS MADE EXCLUSIVELY BY HUMAN BEINGS and can therefore have 'ANY CONTENT WHATSOEVER'. This is LEGAL POSITIVISM, whose line can be traced back to PLATO. THAT SENTENCE ABOUT 'ANY CONTENT' IS EXACTLY WHAT MAKES POSITIVISM CONTESTED: it means that the validity of a norm does not depend on its content, so that even an unjust statute is law — and precisely this dispute came alive again after 1945 over the Nazi statutes. And since the object and the method of regulation are hard to tell apart, especially historically (LAW AGAINST MORALITY, CUSTOM, RELIGION, TECHNICAL STANDARDS), the exercise offers THOMAS RAISER'S conciliatory definition: law is 'A SPECIAL CASE OF SOCIAL NORMS'.

cards.q: Set Pufendorf and Kelsen against each other.
cards.a: PUFENDORF (1632–1694): a legal and just order DERIVED PURELY FROM REASON, therefore UNALTERABLE BY HUMAN BEINGS and valid EQUALLY AND EVERYWHERE — NATURAL LAW, the line running back to ARISTOTLE. KELSEN (1881–1973): LAW IS MADE EXCLUSIVELY BY HUMAN BEINGS and can therefore have 'ANY CONTENT WHATSOEVER' — LEGAL POSITIVISM, the line running back to PLATO.
cards.topic: Introduction: Methods, Sources, Aims of Legal History

cards.q: Why is Kelsen's 'any content whatsoever' contested, and how does Raiser define law?
cards.a: Because it means that THE VALIDITY OF A NORM DOES NOT DEPEND ON ITS CONTENT, so that even an UNJUST STATUTE IS LAW — the dispute revived after 1945 over the Nazi statutes. RAISER offers a conciliatory definition: law is 'A SPECIAL CASE OF SOCIAL NORMS'.

slides.title: Primary and secondary sources, the serving and the own function
slides.text: To the sources the exercise class adds two distinctions that are not in the list of types of source. THE FIRST: PRIMARY SOURCES are original texts or artefacts CREATED AT THE TIME OF THE EVENTS OR CONDITIONS they describe; SECONDARY SOURCES are any text or other source of information about the past that is not a primary source — history books, for instance. The legal historian works with TEXTS (legal texts, medieval chronicles, charters, court files, juristic literature), but sometimes also with MATERIAL OR PHYSICAL SOURCES (legal archaeology), PICTORIAL SOURCES (legal iconography) and ORAL TRADITION. THE SECOND DISTINCTION CONCERNS THE PURPOSE OF THE WHOLE DISCIPLINE and is worth knowing: LEGAL HISTORY HAS A SERVING FUNCTION TOWARDS THE LAW IN FORCE — it helps to understand and interpret it. BUT IT ALSO HAS ITS OWN, INDEPENDENT HISTORICAL VALUE: the method aims at the 'UNDERSTANDING AND EXPLANATION OF PAST REALITIES' (FRANZ WIEACKER). Legal history is therefore not merely an auxiliary science for lawyers.

cards.q: What is the difference between a primary and a secondary source?
cards.a: A PRIMARY source is an original text or artefact CREATED AT THE TIME OF THE EVENTS it describes. A SECONDARY source is any source of information about the past that is not a primary source — a history book, for example.
cards.topic: Introduction: Methods, Sources, Aims of Legal History

cards.q: What double function does legal history have?
cards.a: A SERVING FUNCTION TOWARDS THE LAW IN FORCE — helping to understand and interpret it. And ITS OWN, INDEPENDENT HISTORICAL VALUE: the method aims at the 'UNDERSTANDING AND EXPLANATION OF PAST REALITIES' (FRANZ WIEACKER). It is therefore not merely an auxiliary science for lawyers.
cards.topic: Introduction: Methods, Sources, Aims of Legal History

slides.title: Global legal history: a surplus and a shortage of sources at once
slides.text: The exercise class's answer is sharper than the usual list of difficulties and is worth remembering verbatim, because it is a paradox. AT THE LEVEL OF GLOBAL HISTORY THERE IS SIMULTANEOUSLY A SURPLUS AND A SHORTAGE OF SOURCES: modern bureaucracies produce enormous quantities of documents and the digital world buries us in data, much of which will never be usefully stored or exploited — and at the same time, of a large part of civilizations, cultures and political forms almost nothing has survived. THE SECOND DIFFICULTY: SOME SOURCES CAN BE HANDLED ONLY BY SPECIALISTS, so anyone working at the scale of global history MUST RELY HEAVILY ON COLLEAGUES. THE THIRD, AND DEEPEST: reflecting on law as a special case of normativity is particularly difficult WHEN IT TAKES PLACE IN AN ENTIRELY DIFFERENT HISTORICAL CONTEXT — because every legal formation is coloured by OUR OWN PRECONCEPTIONS, for instance about its relation to religion, ritual, performance, social convention or morality. AND THE CONCLUSION IS HONESTLY SCEPTICAL: SOLUTIONS ARE HARD TO FIND. These are difficulties of TRANSLATION, and in that they are nothing new — they have long occupied historians in the form of the question HOW TO APPROPRIATE THE STRANGENESS OF THE SOURCES CAREFULLY WITHOUT ABOLISHING IT.

cards.q: What paradox holds for sources in global legal history?
cards.a: THERE IS SIMULTANEOUSLY A SURPLUS AND A SHORTAGE: modern bureaucracies and the digital world produce enormous quantities of data, much of which will never be usefully stored — and at the same time, of a large part of civilizations, cultures and political forms ALMOST NOTHING HAS SURVIVED.
cards.topic: Introduction: Methods, Sources, Aims of Legal History

cards.q: What is the deepest difficulty of global legal history, and what is the solution?
cards.a: That reflecting on law in an ENTIRELY DIFFERENT HISTORICAL CONTEXT is coloured by OUR OWN PRECONCEPTIONS — about law's relation to religion, ritual, convention or morality. Solutions are HARD TO FIND: these are difficulties of TRANSLATION, and the question is HOW TO APPROPRIATE THE STRANGENESS OF THE SOURCES CAREFULLY WITHOUT ABOLISHING IT.
cards.topic: Introduction: Methods, Sources, Aims of Legal History

slides.title: Exegesis and its five-step scheme
slides.text: THIS IS THE MOST PRACTICAL THING IN THE WHOLE EXERCISE CLASS, BECAUSE IT IS EXACTLY THE PROCEDURE THE EXAM TESTS. EXEGESIS (from the Greek ἐξήγησις) is the CRITICAL EXPLANATION OR INTERPRETATION OF A TEXT and is the principal method of working with a written source. THE FIVE-STEP SCHEME: (1) READ THE LEGAL SOURCE SLOWLY AND CAREFULLY; then look closely at WHAT IS GIVEN AS THE SOURCE of the passage and HOW ITS HEADING READS. (2) WHAT DO YOU KNOW IN GENERAL ABOUT THE SOURCE THE EXTRACT COMES FROM? (3) WHAT TOPICS DOES THE PASSAGE OPEN UP? Try to pick out KEY WORDS in order to determine what the passage is about. (4) HIGHLIGHT THE LEGAL CONCEPTS THAT APPEAR IN THE PASSAGE AND TRY TO EXPLAIN THEM. (5) ONLY NOW ANALYSE THOSE CONCEPTS FROM A LEGAL POINT OF VIEW AND PLACE THEM IN THEIR HISTORICAL CONTEXT. NOTE THE ORDER: FIRST IDENTIFICATION OF THE SOURCE, THEN CONTENT, THEN CONCEPTS, AND ONLY AT THE END INTERPRETATION. The most common mistake in the exam is to start at step five — that is, to talk about context without saying what the text actually is.

terms.def: The critical explanation or interpretation of a text; the principal method of working with a written source.

cards.q: What is exegesis and how does its five-step scheme run?
cards.a: The CRITICAL EXPLANATION OR INTERPRETATION OF A TEXT. 1) Read the source SLOWLY AND CAREFULLY and look at WHAT IS GIVEN AS THE SOURCE and HOW THE HEADING READS. 2) WHAT DO I KNOW IN GENERAL ABOUT THE SOURCE the extract comes from. 3) WHAT TOPICS the passage opens up — pick out KEY WORDS. 4) HIGHLIGHT THE LEGAL CONCEPTS and explain them. 5) Only then ANALYSE THEM LEGALLY AND PLACE THEM IN HISTORICAL CONTEXT.
cards.topic: Introduction: Methods, Sources, Aims of Legal History

cards.q: What is the most common mistake in exegesis in the exam?
cards.a: TO START AT STEP FIVE — that is, to talk about context without saying WHAT THE TEXT ACTUALLY IS. The order of the scheme is deliberate: first IDENTIFICATION OF THE SOURCE, then CONTENT, then CONCEPTS, and only at the end INTERPRETATION.
cards.topic: Introduction: Methods, Sources, Aims of Legal History

slides.title: Prosopography, praxeology, ethnography
slides.text: Three further methods the historian uses, which the exercise class names as an 'extra question'. PROSOPOGRAPHY is the STUDY OF THE COMMON CHARACTERISTICS OF A GROUP OF PEOPLE whose individual biographies are largely untraceable. In practice: I know nothing about the individual judge, but I know that the judges of a given court came from certain families, studied in Bologna and were on average forty years old — and that already says a good deal about the law. PRAXEOLOGY ventures, from the analysis of UNCONSCIOUSLY PERFORMED ACTIONS (PRACTICES), to draw conclusions about the SOCIO-CULTURAL OR POLITICAL STRUCTURE of the society in which they take place. It can be understood as a THEORY OF HUMAN ACTION based on the idea that people act PURPOSIVELY, as opposed to reflex action and other unintentional behaviour. For legal history this means observing WHAT WAS DONE IN COURT, not only what was written. ETHNOGRAPHY is a branch of anthropology and the SYSTEMATIC STUDY OF INDIVIDUAL CULTURES; it examines cultural phenomena FROM THE POINT OF VIEW OF THE SUBJECT STUDIED, that is, from within — which is exactly what global legal history needs if it is to avoid measuring a foreign order by a European yardstick.

cards.q: What is prosopography and what is it good for in legal history?
cards.a: The STUDY OF THE COMMON CHARACTERISTICS OF A GROUP OF PEOPLE whose INDIVIDUAL BIOGRAPHIES ARE UNTRACEABLE. In practice: I know nothing about the individual judge, but I know where the judges came from, where they studied and how old they were — and that already says a good deal about the law.
cards.topic: Introduction: Methods, Sources, Aims of Legal History

cards.q: What is praxeology and what is ethnography?
cards.a: PRAXEOLOGY draws, from the analysis of UNCONSCIOUSLY PERFORMED ACTIONS (PRACTICES), conclusions about the SOCIO-CULTURAL AND POLITICAL STRUCTURE of a society; it is a theory of human action based on people acting PURPOSIVELY. ETHNOGRAPHY is a branch of anthropology, the SYSTEMATIC STUDY OF INDIVIDUAL CULTURES, examining phenomena FROM THE POINT OF VIEW OF THE SUBJECT STUDIED, that is, from within.
cards.topic: Introduction: Methods, Sources, Aims of Legal History

slides.title: The classical periodization with concrete turning points
slides.text: The exercise class gives the periodization with dates, and it is worth knowing them, because they can be asked about directly. PREHISTORY (about 2.5 million years to 1200 BC) — the period of human life BEFORE WRITTEN RECORDS of human activity; it is divided into the Stone, Bronze and Iron Ages. ANTIQUITY (8th century BC, Homer, to the 5th century AD, the end of the Western Roman Empire) is divided into three parts: the ARCHAIC PERIOD (650–480 BC), in which WRITING arises in the Fertile Crescent (Egypt, the Babylonian empires, the Persian empire) and which ends with the GRAECO-PERSIAN WARS (479 BC); the CLASSICAL PERIOD (the rise of Greece and Rome, Alexander's conquest of the Persian empire, Hellenism, the Punic Wars); and the LATE PERIOD until the end of the Western Roman Empire (476). THE MIDDLE AGES (5th century, the end of the Western Roman Empire, to 1500 — with the landmarks 1453 THE FALL OF CONSTANTINOPLE, 1492 THE COMPLETION OF THE RECONQUISTA AND THE DISCOVERY OF AMERICA). THE MODERN PERIOD (from 1500 to the present) is divided into the EARLY MODERN PERIOD (from the end of the Middle Ages to the 19th century) and the MODERN AGE (from the 19th century, with the landmarks of the FRENCH REVOLUTION 1789 and the INDUSTRIAL REVOLUTION). And after the world wars (1918/1945) one speaks of CONTEMPORARY HISTORY (ZEITGESCHICHTE). The critique of this periodization is on the question sheet; here remember above all the dates, because the examiner asks about the turning points.

cards.q: How is antiquity divided and by which dates is it delimited?
cards.a: From the 8th century BC (HOMER) to the 5th century AD (the end of the Western Roman Empire). The ARCHAIC PERIOD (650–480 BC) — WRITING arises in the Fertile Crescent, ending with the GRAECO-PERSIAN WARS (479 BC). The CLASSICAL PERIOD — the rise of Greece and Rome, Alexander, Hellenism, the Punic Wars. The LATE PERIOD to 476.
cards.topic: Introduction: Methods, Sources, Aims of Legal History

cards.q: By which dates are the Middle Ages and the modern period delimited?
cards.a: THE MIDDLE AGES from the 5th century (the end of the Western Roman Empire) to 1500 — with the landmarks 1453 THE FALL OF CONSTANTINOPLE and 1492 THE RECONQUISTA AND THE DISCOVERY OF AMERICA. THE MODERN PERIOD from 1500: the EARLY MODERN PERIOD to the 19th century, the MODERN AGE from the 19th century (the FRENCH REVOLUTION 1789, the INDUSTRIAL REVOLUTION). After the world wars (1918/1945), CONTEMPORARY HISTORY.
cards.topic: Introduction: Methods, Sources, Aims of Legal History

slides.title: The family tree of the imperial title
slides.text: The exercise class shows the title as a TREE THAT BRANCHES OUT GRADUALLY FROM ROME — and that is precisely the answer to the question what 'emperor' means. THE ROOT: THE ROMAN EMPEROR, 1st–4th century AD. THE DIVISION OF 395: the WESTERN EMPEROR (to 476) and the EASTERN EMPEROR. From the eastern branch the BYZANTINE EMPEROR continues UNTIL 1453. From the western branch, after an interruption, arises the ROMAN-GERMAN EMPEROR 800/962–1806 — a double date because in 800 CHARLEMAGNE was crowned and in 962 OTTO I, whereby the title became permanently tied to the East Frankish (German) empire; it ends in 1806 with the dissolution of the Holy Roman Empire. FURTHER BRANCHES: the RUSSIAN EMPEROR (TSAR) 1478–1917, the TURKISH SULTAN to 1922, the EMPEROR OF THE FRENCH 1804–1815 and 1852–1870 (Napoleon I and III), the EMPEROR OF AUSTRIA 1804–1918 and the GERMAN EMPEROR 1871–1918. NON-EUROPEAN EMPERORS fall into two groups, and that distinction is the point: (a) THOSE REGARDED AS EQUAL TO THE EUROPEAN ONES — the NEGUS in Ethiopia (980 BC – 1974), the TENNŌ in Japan (660 BC to the present), the HUANGDI in China (221 BC – 1912), the SHAHANSHAH in Persia (1501–1979), the GREAT MOGUL in India (1526–1858); (b) THOSE CREATED ON THE EUROPEAN MODEL — the Emperor of Abyssinia (a title of the Italian king 1936–1941), the Emperor of Mexico (1864–67), the Emperor of Brazil (1822–1889) and the EMPEROR OF INDIA as a title of the British monarch 1876–1947. THAT SECOND LIST SHOWS THAT IN THE 19TH CENTURY THE TITLE WAS AN INSTRUMENT OF IMPERIAL POLITICS — Victoria became Empress of India so that the British crown would hold, over the Indian princes, a rank they would recognize.

cards.q: Sketch the family tree of the imperial title from Rome onwards.
cards.a: THE ROMAN EMPEROR (1st–4th c.) → THE DIVISION OF 395 into WESTERN (to 476) and EASTERN → from the east the BYZANTINE EMPEROR TO 1453, from the west the ROMAN-GERMAN EMPEROR 800/962–1806 (800 Charlemagne, 962 Otto I, ending with the dissolution of the empire). Further branches: the RUSSIAN TSAR 1478–1917, the TURKISH SULTAN to 1922, the EMPEROR OF THE FRENCH 1804–15 and 1852–70, the EMPEROR OF AUSTRIA 1804–1918, the GERMAN EMPEROR 1871–1918.
cards.topic: Introduction: Methods, Sources, Aims of Legal History

cards.q: How are non-European emperors divided, and what follows from that?
cards.a: 1) THOSE REGARDED AS EQUAL TO THE EUROPEAN ONES: the NEGUS in Ethiopia, the TENNŌ in Japan (660 BC to the present), the HUANGDI in China (to 1912), the SHAHANSHAH in Persia (1501–1979), the GREAT MOGUL in India (1526–1858). 2) THOSE CREATED ON THE EUROPEAN MODEL: the Emperor of Mexico (1864–67), of Brazil (1822–1889), of Abyssinia, and the EMPEROR OF INDIA as a title of the British monarch 1876–1947. The second list shows that the title was an INSTRUMENT OF IMPERIAL POLITICS.

slides.title: Austria: three meanings and the road to a single state
slides.text: THREE MEANINGS the exercise class expressly distinguishes: (1) THE ORIGINAL, TERRITORIAL MEANING — the 'LAND' of Austria, that is, the march and then the duchy, divided along the river ENNS into Austria above and Austria below the Enns; (2) THE DYNASTIC MEANING — the 'CASA DE AUSTRIA', that is, the HOUSE OF HABSBURG, where 'Austria' means not a territory but a family; (3) THE EXTENDED, TERRITORIAL MEANING — the HABSBURG STATES or 'Austrian lands', collectively the 'HERRSCHAFT ZU ÖSTERREICH', that is, everything the Habsburgs rule. THE ROAD TO A SINGLE STATE: 1526/27 THE ACQUISITION OF THE BOHEMIAN CROWN (the crown of St Wenceslas) and the HUNGARIAN CROWN (the crown of St Stephen) — from then on the Habsburgs hold three crowns, but EACH SEPARATELY, and in each land a different law applies. 1740–1790 THE REFORMS OF MARIA THERESA AND JOSEPH II MERGE THE HABSBURG KINGDOMS AND LANDS INTO A SINGLE OVERALL STATE — legally the most important step, because only then does a unified administration, judiciary and legislation come into being. 1804 THE AUSTRIAN EMPIRE (Francis II assumes the title Emperor of Austria in response to Napoleon, and two years later the Holy Roman Empire is dissolved). 1867 THE AUSTRO-HUNGARIAN MONARCHY. 1918 THE COLLAPSE OF THE MONARCHY. Then: 1918 'GERMAN-AUSTRIA', 1919 'AUSTRIA'; 1918–1933 a DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC, the FIRST REPUBLIC; 1934–1938 the AUTHORITARIAN STATE; 1938–1945 PART OF NAZI GERMANY ('OSTMARK', then the 'Alpine and Danube Gaue'); FROM 1945 THE REPUBLIC OF AUSTRIA, the SECOND REPUBLIC.

terms.def: The dynastic meaning of 'Austria' — the House of Habsburg, not a territory.

cards.q: What three meanings does 'Austria' have?
cards.a: 1) THE ORIGINAL, TERRITORIAL one — the 'LAND' of Austria (the march, then the duchy), divided along the ENNS. 2) THE DYNASTIC one — the 'CASA DE AUSTRIA', the HOUSE OF HABSBURG, not a territory. 3) THE EXTENDED, TERRITORIAL one — the HABSBURG STATES or 'Austrian lands', collectively the 'HERRSCHAFT ZU ÖSTERREICH'.
cards.topic: Introduction: Methods, Sources, Aims of Legal History

cards.q: When did the Habsburg lands become a single state, and why does that matter legally?
cards.a: THROUGH THE REFORMS OF MARIA THERESA AND JOSEPH II IN 1740–1790 the kingdoms and lands merge into a SINGLE OVERALL STATE. It matters legally because ONLY THEN DOES A UNIFIED ADMINISTRATION, JUDICIARY AND LEGISLATION COME INTO BEING — until then the ruler held each crown separately and each land had its own law (1526/27 the acquisition of the Bohemian and Hungarian crowns).
cards.topic: Introduction: Methods, Sources, Aims of Legal History

cards.q: Name the Austrian state formations from 1804 to the present.
cards.a: 1804 THE AUSTRIAN EMPIRE; 1867 THE AUSTRO-HUNGARIAN MONARCHY; 1918 THE COLLAPSE and 'German-Austria', 1919 'Austria'; 1918–1933 THE FIRST REPUBLIC; 1934–1938 THE AUTHORITARIAN STATE; 1938–1945 PART OF NAZI GERMANY ('Ostmark'); FROM 1945 THE SECOND REPUBLIC.
cards.topic: Introduction: Methods, Sources, Aims of Legal History

slides.title: A worked exegesis I: identifying the source (the May Laws of 1868)
slides.text: The exercise class performs the whole procedure on a real source, so it is worth going through it step by step as a model. THE SOURCE: 'Art. II. If one of the clergymen called upon under the provisions of the General Civil Code to publish the banns refuses to publish them, or if one of the clergymen called upon to receive the solemn declaration of consent, having been requested to do so by the betrothed, refuses to publish the banns or to receive the solemn declaration of consent to the marriage ON THE GROUND OF AN IMPEDIMENT NOT RECOGNIZED BY STATE LEGISLATION, the betrothed may have the banns of their marriage published by the SECULAR AUTHORITY and make the solemn declaration of consent BEFORE THAT AUTHORITY.' (Reichs-Gesetz-Blatt für das Kaiserthum Oesterreich 1868, no. 47.) STEP 1 — WHAT IS GIVEN AS THE SOURCE AND HOW THE HEADING READS: a STATUTE OF MAY 1868, published in the IMPERIAL LAW GAZETTE FOR THE AUSTRIAN EMPIRE. That double finding alone (the date and the collection) already delimits a great deal: it is an imperial, that is, an all-Cisleithanian enactment, and it dates from shortly after the December Constitution. STEP 2 — WHAT I KNOW ABOUT THE SOURCE IN GENERAL: it is one of the so-called MAY LAWS OF 1868, issued IN THE WAKE OF THE BASIC LAW ON THE GENERAL RIGHTS OF CITIZENS OF 1867, in order to regulate anew the RELATION OF STATE AND CHURCH. In practice THE MAY LAWS PUNCHED HOLES IN THE CONCORDAT OF 1855, which was then FORMALLY ABROGATED IN 1870 (Austria denounced it after the First Vatican Council proclaimed the dogma of papal infallibility). The statute returned marriage law for Catholics to the ABGB and transferred jurisdiction in Catholic matrimonial matters to the SECULAR AUTHORITIES, that is, the courts.

cards.q: What are the May Laws of 1868 and what did they do to the Concordat?
cards.a: Statutes issued IN THE WAKE OF THE BASIC LAW ON THE GENERAL RIGHTS OF CITIZENS OF 1867 in order to regulate anew the RELATION OF STATE AND CHURCH. In practice they PUNCHED HOLES IN THE CONCORDAT OF 1855, which was FORMALLY ABROGATED IN 1870. They returned marriage law for Catholics to the ABGB and transferred jurisdiction in matrimonial matters to the SECULAR COURTS.
cards.topic: Introduction: Methods, Sources, Aims of Legal History

slides.title: A worked exegesis II: topic, concepts, interpretation
slides.text: STEP 3 — WHAT TOPICS THE PASSAGE OPENS UP AND THE KEY WORD: the key word is 'RELATIVE NOTZIVILEHE', that is, the CIVIL MARRIAGE OF NECESSITY or in exceptional cases. It means that under certain conditions — for instance where the betrothed do not share the same religious denomination — the statute provided for a CIVIL MARRIAGE concluded before a SECULAR PUBLIC AUTHORITY. IT WAS THE FIRST STEP TOWARDS CIVIL MARRIAGE IN AUSTRIA. The word 'relative' matters here: civil marriage WAS NOT GENERALLY AVAILABLE, but only as a FALLBACK where the clergyman refused the act on a ground the state does not recognize. STEP 4 — THE LEGAL CONCEPTS: 'AUFGEBOT', the BANNS — the PUBLIC ANNOUNCEMENT OF AN INTENDED MARRIAGE, whose purpose is TO ALLOW ANYONE TO RAISE AN IMPEDIMENT and thereby prevent void marriages. Further, the 'solemn declaration of consent' (the act of concluding the marriage itself) and the 'impediment not recognized by state legislation' (a canonical impediment the state does not treat as legally relevant — typically difference of denomination). STEP 5 — LEGAL ANALYSIS AND HISTORICAL CONTEXT: the marriage law of the ABGB was FORMALLY STATE LAW, but IN SUBSTANCE IT RESTED ON THE PRINCIPLE OF DENOMINATIONAL MARRIAGE — both the banns and the marriage had to take place BEFORE A PRIEST, who was, however, ACTING AS AN ORGAN OF THE STATE. That is the peculiar construction one must be able to state: the state kept the law for itself but entrusted its execution to the church. THE PRINCIPLE OF DENOMINATIONAL MARRIAGE LASTED LONGER IN AUSTRIA THAN IN MOST EUROPEAN COUNTRIES, RIGHT UP TO 1938. ONLY IN 1939, AFTER THE ANNEXATION OF AUSTRIA TO GERMANY, WAS THE MARRIAGE ACT WITH THE PRINCIPLE OF COMPULSORY CIVIL MARRIAGE INTRODUCED HERE. That is the point to remember, uncomfortable as it is: COMPULSORY CIVIL MARRIAGE CAME TO AUSTRIA WITH THE NAZI ANNEXATION, and it nevertheless remained after 1945.

terms.def: Civil marriage of necessity — available only where a clergyman refuses the act on a ground the state does not recognize.

cards.q: What is 'relative Notzivilehe' and why is it 'relative'?
cards.a: The CIVIL MARRIAGE OF NECESSITY: under certain conditions — for instance where the betrothed are of different denominations — the statute provided for a marriage before a SECULAR AUTHORITY. It is 'relative' because civil marriage WAS NOT GENERALLY AVAILABLE but only a FALLBACK where the clergyman refused the act on a ground the state does not recognize. It was the FIRST STEP TOWARDS CIVIL MARRIAGE IN AUSTRIA.
cards.topic: Introduction: Methods, Sources, Aims of Legal History

cards.q: What is the 'Aufgebot', the banns, and what is its purpose?
cards.a: The PUBLIC ANNOUNCEMENT OF AN INTENDED MARRIAGE, whose purpose is TO ALLOW ANYONE TO RAISE AN IMPEDIMENT and thereby PREVENT VOID MARRIAGES.
cards.topic: Introduction: Methods, Sources, Aims of Legal History

cards.q: On what principle did the marriage law of the ABGB rest, and how long did it last?
cards.a: It was FORMALLY STATE LAW but IN SUBSTANCE RESTED ON THE PRINCIPLE OF DENOMINATIONAL MARRIAGE — banns and marriage took place BEFORE A PRIEST, who was however ACTING AS AN ORGAN OF THE STATE. The principle lasted in Austria LONGER THAN IN MOST OF EUROPE, UP TO 1938; only in 1939, AFTER THE ANNEXATION TO GERMANY, was the Marriage Act with COMPULSORY CIVIL MARRIAGE introduced — and it remained after 1945.
cards.topic: Introduction: Methods, Sources, Aims of Legal History
